text:
raj: Heads-up — noticed a p95 latency jump on prod-hosted-us-west around 08:05 UTC. Correlates with the Triton 2.1.7 deploy.
perf-bot: ALERT p95_tokens_latency increased from 78ms -> 210ms on prod-hosted-us-west (window 08:00-08:10)
raj: Minimal traffic change, throughput steady. Looks like more GPU kernel switchbacks in traces.
sasha: Can you paste the span ids or an example request? Might be KV cache churn.
raj: Here’s a trace dump (redacted):
```
kernel_seq: flash_attn_fwd -> gemm_tiled -> cudnn_lstm
nvlink_latency: +12ms
kv_evictions: spike from 2/min -> 28/min
batch_sizes: median 3 -> 1.6
```
eli: median batch size dropping explains lower kernel efficiency. Did the autoselect change try to favor smaller workspace kernels? maya: I rolled the autoselect heuristic change to canary last night (shortseq tie-breaker tweak). It matches the deploy time.
raj: That lines up. Also seeing more PCIe stalls on a subset of hosts, noisy-tenant maybe.
sasha: Could be two things interacting: kernel selector preferring non-flash kernels for short seqs, + noisy neighbor causing higher PCIe latency so KV lookups slow -> evictions -> smaller batches.
perf-bot: Perf profile attached: /s3/prof/prod/1969971234/nvprof-summary.txt
maya: Quick repro on bench: run batcher with seq_len distribution [8,12,16] and enable new selector. Command: `./bench_client --dist short --selector canary --profile nvprof.out`
eli: I ran that locally, saw flash_attn_fwd usage drop 70% and p95 increase 3x. Attaching snippet: `nvprof: flash_attn_fwd 120ms -> gemm_tiled 320ms`.
raj: Ops, can we try forcing kernel preference back to flash on one canary node? env var `RED_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_flash` exists right?
ops-bot: Rolling restart initiated on prod-hosted-us-west-canary-3 with RED_KERNEL_POLICY=prefer_flash (triggered by @raj)
ops-bot: Restart complete. Observability: p95 tokens latency dropped back to 85ms on canary-3 in 2 minutes.
sasha: Good signal. That suggests the selector tie-break change is the root cause. But we still saw KV eviction spike — maybe kernel choice affects execution time -> longer KV hold times -> eviction pressure.
maya: The selector change was trying to reduce workspace memory by preferring tiled GEMM for short seqs, thought it'd save memory; didn't account for KV cache lifetime interaction.
eli: Actionable: 1) revert canary-wide selector change; 2) add a guard: for models with KV enabled, prefer flash when seq<64 and batch>1; 3) run synthetic microbench across short/medium seqs.
raj: Agree. Also add a metric that ties kernel_id -> kv_eviction_rate so we can detect this faster.
sasha: I'll open a quick PR for the guard and a perf test. `PR: github.com/redwood/serving@pr/ker-tiebreaker-rollback`
maya: Reverting the canary now and scheduling a full rollback if other canaries show same pattern.
ops-bot: Canary revert deployed to canary group. Monitoring 15 minutes.
perf-bot: After revert, global p95 back to baseline 82-90ms. KV evictions down.
raj: Follow-ups: postmortem note, add kernel->kv correlation dashboard, and add an automatic fallback that pins kernel by model when eviction_rate>10/min.
eli: Also let's capture nsight timeline for one affected host to confirm PCIe/noisy neighbor role. I suspect both factors compounded.
sasha: Will do. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
